tables.title: Contrary evidence and what would change the view

rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- High: the covenant levels, step-downs and definitions of the maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio and the minimum Interest Coverage Ratio are not in the sources, so covenant headroom cannot be calculated and the issuer's leverage ratios cannot be tied to the covenant ratio; the executed credit agreement and its amendment would close it. - High: pre-acquisition EBITDA behind the issuer's acquisition-adjusted EBITDA is not itemized by acquired business or period, so the 2.3x ratio cannot be rebuilt and the USD 88.8 million uplift is unverified; the acquired businesses' trailing twelve-month EBITDA would close it. - Medium: cash paid for interest is printed only in the annual report, so interest cover is stated for FY2024 and FY2025 and not for any 2026 period; the quarterly cash interest would close it. - Medium: no adjusted EBITDA is stated for FY2024, so adjusted leverage and cover for that year are not calculable; the FY2024 annual report or release would close it. - Medium: the sources hold no 2025 interim balance sheets, so net debt and leverage for 2025-03-31, 2025-06-30 and 2025-09-30 are not stated, and the 2025 interim columns of the balance sheet are omitted; the 2025 quarterly reports would close it. - Medium: the 2024 and 2025 cash flow statements include discontinued operations that the filings do not segregate, so operating cash flow, free cash flow and cash interest for those periods are on a wider perimeter than continuing operations; the filings print no split. - Medium: the instrument-level carrying values, the post-amendment margin grid, any interest rate floor and the lien ranking between the term loan B and the revolver are not stated, so the spread, floor and ranking cells of the debt instrument table are not supplied. - Medium: the purchase price of Test Logic, acquired on 2026-10-05, is not stated, so the pro forma net debt and net leverage for it are not established; a later filing would close it. - Low: the balance sheet at 2024-12-31 shows cash of USD 29.505m while the cash flow statement ends FY2024 at USD 29.030m, a difference of USD 0.475m that the annual report does not explain; the debt tables use the balance-sheet figure. - Low: several statement lines are printed as a dash or are absent from some periods and are shown as not supplied rather than zero: earn-out fair value adjustments, lease abandonment costs, the loss on debt extinguishment, impairment, sale proceeds, purchases of intangible assets, life insurance proceeds, amortizing note repayments, tangible equity unit proceeds, other financing, held-for-sale balances, the note receivable, deferred tax liabilities and the earn-out obligation in the periods where they do not appear. - Low: no fourth-quarter 2025 report is in the sources, so Q4 2025 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA are calculated as the fiscal year less nine months; the Q4 2025 release would close it. - Low: capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, and no segment revenue exists because the issuer reports one segment, so the segment schedule is empty and no segment sum is stated. - Low: the FY2023 balance sheet is outside the annual report's two-year balance sheet, so FY2023 leverage is not stated, and the FY2025 and FY2024 statements are the only fiscal years in the statement tables. - Low: EBITDA for FY2024 and FY2025 is calculated because the annual report states none, and the issuer's own EBITDA from continuing operations appears only in the 2026 releases.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view

facts.label: Key findings

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a more favourable view is that management's own measures show deleveraging: adjusted net leverage was 2.4x at 2026-06-30 and 2.3x at 2026-09-30, Q3 free cash flow was USD 46.6 million, margin guidance has been raised twice, and at the guided year-end Adjusted EBITDA a flat net debt would give 2.58x to 2.53x. If the fourth quarter delivers free cash flow that repays the revolver, if the pre-acquisition earnings are itemized and hold near USD 88.8 million, and if the covenant levels prove wide, the view would move toward a stronger business profile with adequate liquidity. It would turn weaker if fourth-quarter revenue falls below the guidance-implied USD 520.5 million, if inventory keeps building without cash conversion, or if the covenant levels sit close to current ratios; a 20% fall in Adjusted EBITDA alone, with net debt unchanged, would take net leverage to 3.72x. facts.text: VSE Corporation is a Delaware company based in Miramar, Florida, listed on NASDAQ, that distributes aviation aftermarket parts and repairs engine, auxiliary power unit, avionics and airframe components as one reportable segment. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is transactional aftermarket parts and repair work, and it is cyclical: the annual report states the aviation industry has been subject to downward cycles that lower demand for engine and component parts and repair and raise credit risk. Organic growth of about 15%, 14% and 17% in the first three quarters of 2026 was attributed to commercial engine aftermarket activity, newly awarded OEM distribution agreements and share gains, and the issuer holds exclusive manufacturing, distribution and repair rights over certain fuel control systems and PT6 fuel pumps. The risk is that distribution revenue rests on OEM agreements whose terms are not supplied, and one customer group was about 20% of FY2025 revenue, roughly USD 222.5 million, and the annual report warns that results would suffer if lost business could not be replaced in time on comparable terms while leases and inventory remain. Pricing power is not evidenced: the annual report lists inflation without contractual protection and tariffs as risks, and no price and volume split is disclosed. Creditors should treat revenue as demand-driven and moderately concentrated, with no contracted floor. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: The income statement does not separate fixed and variable cost, but the pattern points to meaningful operating leverage: revenue less cost of services rose from 10.10% to 14.86% in nine months as repair scale grew, and revenue less cost of products from 15.84% to 19.00%. Repair brings labour, certified facilities and capacity commitments, substantially all of the facilities are leased, and the annual report names skilled labour and inflation without contract protection as risks. The mechanism is that the same operating leverage works in reverse if volume falls, so margins are defensible in a moderate slowdown but not proven in a downturn. Reported EBITDA also moves with non-cash items: an earn-out fair value gain of USD 8.9 million sits in 2026 reported EBITDA against a charge of USD 29.2 million in nine months 2025, and management's add-backs lift nine-month Adjusted EBITDA USD 27.1 million over reported, so Adjusted EBITDA is the better trend measure but carries management's judgement. facts.label: Capital intensity and cash conversion
facts.text: Capital intensity is low and is not what limits cash flow: capital expenditure was USD 31.5 million over the last twelve months, 1.95% of revenue, and the issuer does not split maintenance from growth spending, so capex flexibility cannot be separated from growth plans. Working capital is the drain: inventory rose USD 339.2 million since year-end to 55.26% of last-twelve-months revenue, with USD 148.4 million of cash purchases and USD 200.2 million acquired with PAG, and management ties the purchases to a new OEM auxiliary power unit programme and engine initiatives. Interest is the second claim: estimated contractual interest is USD 57.7 million a year before swaps and fees, and cash interest and cash taxes for 2026 are not stated, while FY2025 cash interest was USD 26.8 million and cash taxes USD 16.1 million. Two claims sit outside the debt figure: the earn-out liability of USD 27.4 million, which the issuer may settle in cash or equity, and long-term operating lease obligations of USD 75.8 million; the annual report says finance leases are not material, and the sources mention no pension, factoring or supply-chain finance obligation. Free cash flow was USD 46.6 million in Q3 and USD -50.0 million in the first half, so EBITDA is converting to cash unevenly, and deleveraging over the next four quarters will come mainly from EBITDA growth unless inventory growth stops. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry limits pricing power. The annual report describes a fragmented industry with intense competition, many competitors larger and better resourced than VSE, and OEMs and certified repair facilities that may bundle services. The consequence is that margin gains must come from mix and proprietary repair approvals rather than scale, which is how the third-quarter release frames the Atech purchase, with sole-source repairs on flight-critical parts. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The liquidity effect is limited within two years: USD 545.0 million is 6.03x 2027 scheduled claims, no principal beyond amortization is due before the amortizing notes end in 2029, and the revolver matures in 2030. The refinancing effect arrives through covenants and cost: if the maximum net leverage ratio or the minimum interest coverage ratio tightened, the revolver could be restricted when it is most needed, and a fall in EBITDA would also raise the interest margin on the floating-rate debt, which the credit agreement ties to the leverage ratio. Management's levers are real: it can slow inventory purchases, pay the earn-out in shares, keep the dividend at USD 0.10 per share a quarter, which cost USD 8.0 million over nine months, defer acquisitions and trim capital expenditure of USD 31.5 million. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through the maturity horizon, but not to hold leverage near 3x; the evidence supports no default path and supports a path of slower deleveraging and covenant pressure. Primary downside path: weaker engine aftermarket demand strands inventory and under-uses new repair capacity while debt and interest stay fixed. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, VSE presents an adequate business profile supported by an equity-funded balance sheet, exclusive OEM rights and certified repair capability, and record margins, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 2.98x to 3.38x on earnings that include unverified add-backs, free cash flow close to zero and an intangible-heavy asset base. Cash-flow durability is not fully assessable yet because only one quarter has converted well, and the business profile cannot be ranked against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector because no peer data is supplied. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on keeping liquidity of about USD 545.0 million intact, delivering a fourth quarter of strong cash flow and the covenant levels leaving room, with the large maturity in 2033 and the revolver in 2030. The primary downside path is weaker engine aftermarket demand that strands inventory while debt and interest stay fixed. Further analysis would require the credit agreement with covenant levels, the pre-acquisition earnings by acquired business, ratings and market pricing, and the proxy statement. Top risk: leverage that rests on unverified earnings and thin cash conversion. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C1; calculation C14; calculation C10; calculation C17

## Request

VSE CORP (issuer vsec), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module checks whether the seven supplied filings and earnings releases, which run from the FY2025 annual report to the Q3 2026 quarterly report, can support the requested analysis of the issuer's business and governance, financial foundation and fundamental credit. The reporting entity is VSE Corporation and its subsidiaries on a consolidated basis.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsec-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (unaudited) | 2026-08-06 (signature date) | fa3609d44d226dc8671529fb2fbfc175fcb641b5ffc98070769608107bc75600 | First statements with PAG consolidated, term loan B note, exhibit list naming the credit agreement amendment |

No earlier module output was supplied: this module is the first of the run.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and earnings releases support a dated credit snapshot of VSE CORP, but not covenant headroom, ratings or market-based work, so creditors should read every leverage ratio as management-defined until the credit agreement is supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; calculation C5

The statements and releases tie on the figures that drive leverage: principal debt of USD 978.8 million and net debt of USD 894.2 million in the Q3 release reproduce from the quarterly report's balance sheet and debt note. Management reports net leverage of 3.0x and adjusted net leverage of 2.3x, and the gap between them rests on USD 88.8 million of pre-acquisition EBITDA that no supplied document itemizes. Covenant levels, guarantor and collateral terms, ratings, market prices and the governance disclosures held in the proxy statement are not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; calculation C2; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net debt rose to USD 894.2 million at 2026-09-30 from USD 223.4 million at year-end 2025, so net leverage on reported EBITDA is now 3.38x rather than 1.74x and creditors carry a more levered, acquisition-driven credit than the FY2025 accounts show.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C4; calculation C11

The ratio depends on the denominator: 2.98x on management's adjusted EBITDA and 2.3x on its acquisition-adjusted measure, which adds pre-acquisition earnings that no filing itemizes. Reported EBITDA holds only about five months of PAG, so 3.38x overstates run-rate leverage. Cash generation has not yet funded deleveraging: nine-month operating cash flow was USD 21.3 million after an inventory build of USD 148.4 million. Liquidity is USD 545.0 million of cash and undrawn revolver. The Test Logic purchase on 2026-10-05 is not in these figures and its pro forma effect is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C11; calculation C19
### Leverage trajectory and drivers

Net debt rose USD 670.7 million between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30. The PAG purchase took about USD 1.75 billion of cash on 2026-05-05; equity and tangible equity unit proceeds of about USD 1.3 billion raised in February 2026 and a new USD 900.0 million term loan B paid for it, which is why debt carrying value rose USD 667.1 million while cash barely moved. Net debt over last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 264.2 million went from 1.74x at FY2025 to 3.38x, and over the issuer's adjusted EBITDA of USD 300.4 million it is 2.98x.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C4; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C25

The ratios mean different things. Reported last-twelve-months EBITDA holds PAG only from 2026-05-05 while debt carries its whole financing, so 3.38x overstates run-rate leverage. The issuer's acquisition-adjusted EBITDA of USD 389.2 million adds USD 88.8 million of pre-acquisition earnings that no filing itemizes or audits, which is how management reaches 2.3x. The evidence supports a range, not one number, and the covenant ratio that governs the facility is defined differently again and its level is not supplied.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C6; calculation C27
### Coverage and interest burden

Cash paid for interest was USD 26.8 million in FY2025 against reported EBITDA of USD 128.8 million, which is cover of 4.80x, up from 2.27x in FY2024 after the revolver was repaid from the Fleet sale proceeds and the October 2025 equity offering. No quarterly report states cash interest, and nine-month 2026 net interest expense of USD 17.9 million is flattered by interest income earned on cash held before the PAG closing. At the 2026-09-30 rates and balances, contractual interest on the term loan B, revolver and amortizing notes is about USD 57.7 million a year before swaps and fees, so reported EBITDA of USD 264.2 million would cover it about 4.58x. That is an estimate built from stated rates and balances, not a reported ratio.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C11; calculation C20; calculation C21
### Cash-flow quality

Operating cash flow was USD 21.3 million for nine months 2026 after an inventory build of USD 148.4 million, and capital expenditure of USD 24.7 million left free cash flow at USD -3.4 million. The path improved within the year: operating cash flow was USD -34.7 million in the first half and USD 56.0 million in Q3 alone. Inventory is USD 893.0 million, 19.9% of total assets, and the FY2025 audit named the write-down of slow-moving inventory as a critical audit matter, so cash tied up in stock carries valuation risk that a creditor cannot see in the leverage ratios.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C22; calculation C23
### Liquidity and maturities

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is USD 545.0 million, made up of USD 65.8 million of cash and USD 479.2 million of undrawn revolver commitments. The maturity profile is back-ended: the term loan B repays USD 9.0 million a year and the amortizing notes USD 23.7 million in 2027, but USD 841.5 million, 86.0% of principal, falls due at the 2033 term loan maturity. A current earn-out obligation of USD 27.4 million, most of it payable in cash or equity at the company's sole discretion, is a further possible claim on liquidity.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-03-31_vsec-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C16; calculation C19; calculation C24
### Definitions and data quality

Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA exceeds reported EBITDA by USD 27.1 million because management adds back acquisition and integration costs, stock-based compensation and a refinancing loss and deducts a non-cash earn-out gain; the add-backs are management's and are not independently verified. The acquisition consideration appears as a headline of about USD 2.025 billion, as purchase consideration that includes the earn-out at fair value, and as cash paid net of cash acquired; each is kept for its own use. Cash flow statements include discontinued operations for 2025 periods, so 2025 free cash flow does not match the continuing perimeter. Purchase price allocations for PAG, NorthStar and Atech are preliminary.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C26
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for lower leverage is operating momentum: Q3 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 107.2 million is the highest quarter on record and management guides FY2026 revenue growth of 65% to 66.5%. If the strong fourth-quarter cash generation that management expects is delivered and the pre-acquisition EBITDA is itemized, the 2.3x measure would be credible. If inventory keeps building without cash conversion, or the covenant levels leave little room, the reported 3.38x is the better guide.

## Gaps

- High: the covenant levels, step-downs and definitions of the maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio and the minimum Interest Coverage Ratio are not in the sources, so covenant headroom cannot be calculated and the issuer's leverage ratios cannot be tied to the covenant ratio; the executed credit agreement and its amendment would close it.

- High: pre-acquisition EBITDA behind the issuer's acquisition-adjusted EBITDA is not itemized by acquired business or period, so the 2.3x ratio cannot be rebuilt and the USD 88.8 million uplift is unverified; the acquired businesses' trailing twelve-month EBITDA would close it.
- Medium: cash paid for interest is printed only in the annual report, so interest cover is stated for FY2024 and FY2025 and not for any 2026 period; the quarterly cash interest would close it.
- Medium: no adjusted EBITDA is stated for FY2024, so adjusted leverage and cover for that year are not calculable; the FY2024 annual report or release would close it.

- Medium: the sources hold no 2025 interim balance sheets, so net debt and leverage for 2025-03-31, 2025-06-30 and 2025-09-30 are not stated, and the 2025 interim columns of the balance sheet are omitted; the 2025 quarterly reports would close it.

- Medium: the 2024 and 2025 cash flow statements include discontinued operations that the filings do not segregate, so operating cash flow, free cash flow and cash interest for those periods are on a wider perimeter than continuing operations; the filings print no split.

- Medium: the instrument-level carrying values, the post-amendment margin grid, any interest rate floor and the lien ranking between the term loan B and the revolver are not stated, so the spread, floor and ranking cells of the debt instrument table are not supplied.
- Medium: the purchase price of Test Logic, acquired on 2026-10-05, is not stated, so the pro forma net debt and net leverage for it are not established; a later filing would close it.

- Low: the balance sheet at 2024-12-31 shows cash of USD 29.505m while the cash flow statement ends FY2024 at USD 29.030m, a difference of USD 0.475m that the annual report does not explain; the debt tables use the balance-sheet figure.

- Low: several statement lines are printed as a dash or are absent from some periods and are shown as not supplied rather than zero: earn-out fair value adjustments, lease abandonment costs, the loss on debt extinguishment, impairment, sale proceeds, purchases of intangible assets, life insurance proceeds, amortizing note repayments, tangible equity unit proceeds, other financing, held-for-sale balances, the note receivable, deferred tax liabilities and the earn-out obligation in the periods where they do not appear.
- Low: no fourth-quarter 2025 report is in the sources, so Q4 2025 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA are calculated as the fiscal year less nine months; the Q4 2025 release would close it.

- Low: capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, and no segment revenue exists because the issuer reports one segment, so the segment schedule is empty and no segment sum is stated.

- Low: the FY2023 balance sheet is outside the annual report's two-year balance sheet, so FY2023 leverage is not stated, and the FY2025 and FY2024 statements are the only fiscal years in the statement tables.
- Low: EBITDA for FY2024 and FY2025 is calculated because the annual report states none, and the issuer's own EBITDA from continuing operations appears only in the 2026 releases.

## Findings
### Bottom line

VSE is an acquisition-built aviation aftermarket company with no disclosed sponsor or controlling holder, so creditors rely on management's equity-funded acquisition record and PAG integration rather than owner support, and governance evidence is thin.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; calculation C11

Nine-month 2026 revenue was USD 1,314.7 million, up 62.09%, and PAG supplied USD 278.2 million of it after closing on 2026-05-05. Equity and equity-linked units raised about USD 1.3 billion, which limited debt-funded growth, yet debt still rose to USD 959.9 million. One customer group was 20% of FY2025 revenue and inventory is USD 893.0 million. The proxy statement is not supplied, so board, ownership and pay facts are not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C1; calculation C15
### Key findings

The business is a single-segment aviation aftermarket platform in which repair has overtaken distribution. Repair revenue was USD 318.0 million and distribution USD 223.0 million in Q3 2026, against distribution at 63.29% of FY2025 revenue, mainly because of the PAG acquisition. Customers are almost entirely commercial, with government customers at 1.10% of Q3 revenue.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C3; calculation C4

Concentration is moderate but real. One affiliated customer group was 20% of FY2025 revenue and the United States was 56.61% and Canada 13.40%, so one relationship could remove a fifth of revenue while facility and inventory carrying costs stay. The 2026 reports do not update the customer share.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C5; calculation C15

Growth is acquisition-led and funded with a high share of equity, which supports creditors, but integration is the main business risk. Six businesses were acquired between 2025-05-01 and 2026-10-05, including PAG at USD 2,020.0 million of purchase consideration, and about USD 1.3 billion of equity and equity-linked units covered most of the USD 1.75 billion cash price. Reported growth of 62.09% includes acquired revenue; pro forma growth as if PAG had been owned throughout 2025 was 22.81% and the issuer puts Q3 organic growth at about 17%.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C1; calculation C7; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C15

No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, so stress support would have to come from public equity markets rather than an owner. The PAG seller will hold about 4.80% of the share count once its exchangeable subsidiary shares convert, automatically by 2029-05-05, and tangible equity unit holders receive shares from 2029-02-01; the sources state no board or veto rights for either, and the proxy statement that would show them is not supplied.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsec-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; calculation C6

Financial policy is acquisitive but shareholder payouts are small. Dividends were USD 8.0 million in nine months 2026, 3.20% of Adjusted EBITDA, there were no repurchases beyond shares forfeited to cover employee taxes, and the credit agreement limits dividends annually, so leakage to equity is not the concern; repeated debt-supported deals are.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C9

Asset quality depends on judgements a creditor cannot test. Inventory is 19.93% of total assets and goodwill and intangibles are 62.59%, the FY2025 audit named slow-moving inventory write-downs as a critical audit matter, and purchase price allocations for the acquired businesses remain preliminary, so a write-down would cut equity and earnings without adding cash.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–12; calculation C8

Governance reporting is adequate for monitoring but incomplete for control. The sources show regular quarterly reporting, effective disclosure controls and a fair-presentation audit opinion, while controls at four acquired businesses are still being integrated, and board composition, independence, ownership and pay are not established.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the funding record: about USD 1.3 billion of equity and equity-linked units covered most of the USD 1.75 billion PAG cash price, no related-party fees, distributions beyond a small dividend or creditor-adverse actions appear in the sources, and the chief executive's disclosed sale plan covers about 0.12% of shares outstanding. A proxy statement that shows a holder with board or veto rights, a credit agreement with wide restricted-payment and investment baskets, or pre-acquisition earnings well below management's adjusted measure would push governance risk toward High. Disclosure of the acquired businesses' earnings that matches management's view and a clean fourth-quarter integration would move it toward Low.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsec-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C16
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that no holder controls the company rests on the absence of any control disclosure in the filings and would change if the proxy shows a holder with board or veto rights.

- The credit agreement is not supplied, so the conclusion that financial policy is acquisitive but bounded is untested; wide restricted-payment, investment or unrestricted-subsidiary baskets would make it more adverse.

- PAG's results before 2026-05-05 are available only as unaudited pro forma revenue and net income, so the underlying growth reading of 22.81% rests on an issuer-prepared pro forma; a materially different stand-alone history would change it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C7

- Customer concentration is stated for FY2025 only, so the 20% share may be stale after PAG and Aero 3 broadened the base; a lower share would reduce the concentration conclusion and a higher one would sharpen it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C15
- The annual report describes PAG as pending, so its risk factors predate the closing; the 2026 quarterly reports state no material change, which this module accepts as stated.
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The PAG acquisition closed on 2026-05-05 with purchase consideration of USD 2,020.0 million, made up of cash net of cash acquired of USD 1.75 billion, equity in a VSE subsidiary and an earn-out of up to USD 125.000 million recorded at fair value. The headline of about USD 2.025 billion in the annual report and releases is a different definition of the same price.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C12

Funding came in three layers. Common stock and tangible equity units raised about USD 1.3 billion in February 2026. The amended senior secured credit agreement added a USD 900.000 million term loan B due 2033-05-05, repaid the prior term loan and raised the revolver commitment from USD 400.000 million to USD 500.000 million due 2030-05-02. The tangible equity units also carry senior unsecured amortizing notes at 5.93% that amortize to 2029-02-01. Debt carrying value rose USD 667.1 million to USD 959.9 million by 2026-09-30.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–29; calculation C10; calculation C11

Three smaller acquisitions bracket PAG: NorthStar on 2026-04-01 before it, and Atech on 2026-08-31, paid partly from the revolver, and Test Logic on 2026-10-05 after it; the Test Logic price is not stated and the deal is not in any period figure.

## Gaps

- High: the proxy statement for the 2026 annual meeting is not supplied, so board composition, independence, committee roles, compensation and beneficial ownership are not established; the control and alignment conclusions are bounded until it is obtained.

- High: the executed credit agreement, its first amendment and the note indenture are not supplied, so legal capacity for dividends, investments, liens and unrestricted subsidiaries cannot be separated from willingness; the behaviour assessment is limited to documented actions.
- High: pre-acquisition earnings of PAG and the other acquired businesses are not itemized, so underlying growth and scale rest on an unaudited pro forma revenue and net income table.
- Medium: customer concentration is not updated after FY2025, so the 20% customer group may be stale after PAG and Aero 3.
- Medium: the timing and form of the PAG earn-out payment are not stated, so the liquidity and dilution effect is not established.
- Medium: whether any holder exercises control is not confirmed, because the filings contain no control disclosure and the proxy statement is not supplied.
- Low: the Test Logic purchase price is not stated and the acquisition is a subsequent event kept out of period figures.

- Low: revenue by geography is stated for FY2025 only, so the country shares may be stale; related-party transactions and fees are not captioned in the filings read, so their absence is not proof of none.

## Findings
### Bottom line

VSE is an adequate but newly levered credit: record earnings and USD 545.0 million of liquidity support creditors, while thin cash conversion and undisclosed covenant levels leave deleveraging dependent on a fourth quarter that management has only promised.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C12; calculation C14

Net debt was USD 894.2 million at 2026-09-30, before the Test Logic purchase on 2026-10-05, whose pro forma effect is not established. Net leverage is 3.38x on reported EBITDA and 2.98x on Adjusted EBITDA, against management's 2.3x, which relies on earnings no filing itemizes. Free cash flow was USD -3.4 million in nine months, and guidance implies fourth-quarter revenue below the third quarter. The primary downside path is weaker engine aftermarket demand stranding inventory of USD 893.0 million while debt stays fixed.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C15; calculation C8
### Key findings

Earnings momentum is the main support for creditors, and part of it is organic. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 19.81% in Q3 against 16.74% a year earlier, organic revenue growth was about 15%, 14% and 17% in the first three quarters of 2026, and management raised revenue and margin guidance in both August and November. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a more favourable view is that management's own measures show deleveraging: adjusted net leverage was 2.4x at 2026-06-30 and 2.3x at 2026-09-30, Q3 free cash flow was USD 46.6 million, margin guidance has been raised twice, and at the guided year-end Adjusted EBITDA a flat net debt would give 2.58x to 2.53x. If the fourth quarter delivers free cash flow that repays the revolver, if the pre-acquisition earnings are itemized and hold near USD 88.8 million, and if the covenant levels prove wide, the view would move toward a stronger business profile with adequate liquidity. It would turn weaker if fourth-quarter revenue falls below the guidance-implied USD 520.5 million, if inventory keeps building without cash conversion, or if the covenant levels sit close to current ratios; a 20% fall in Adjusted EBITDA alone, with net debt unchanged, would take net leverage to 3.72x.

### Company description and ownership

VSE Corporation is a Delaware company based in Miramar, Florida, listed on NASDAQ, that distributes aviation aftermarket parts and repairs engine, auxiliary power unit, avionics and airframe components as one reportable segment. Its customers are almost entirely commercial: commercial customers were 98.51% of nine-month revenue, and repair has overtaken distribution at 58.78% of Q3 revenue. Revenue was USD 1,615.9 million over the last twelve months, 2.06x the FY2024 level, so the business has been rebuilt by acquisition since the Fleet and Federal and Defense sales. The credit consequence is that cash flow follows aircraft utilization and maintenance demand, and the scale that supports debt service was bought rather than proven through a full cycle.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is transactional aftermarket parts and repair work, and it is cyclical: the annual report states the aviation industry has been subject to downward cycles that lower demand for engine and component parts and repair and raise credit risk. Organic growth of about 15%, 14% and 17% in the first three quarters of 2026 was attributed to commercial engine aftermarket activity, newly awarded OEM distribution agreements and share gains, and the issuer holds exclusive manufacturing, distribution and repair rights over certain fuel control systems and PT6 fuel pumps. The risk is that distribution revenue rests on OEM agreements whose terms are not supplied, and one customer group was about 20% of FY2025 revenue, roughly USD 222.5 million, and the annual report warns that results would suffer if lost business could not be replaced in time on comparable terms while leases and inventory remain. Pricing power is not evidenced: the annual report lists inflation without contractual protection and tariffs as risks, and no price and volume split is disclosed. Creditors should treat revenue as demand-driven and moderately concentrated, with no contracted floor.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

The income statement does not separate fixed and variable cost, but the pattern points to meaningful operating leverage: revenue less cost of services rose from 10.10% to 14.86% in nine months as repair scale grew, and revenue less cost of products from 15.84% to 19.00%. Repair brings labour, certified facilities and capacity commitments, substantially all of the facilities are leased, and the annual report names skilled labour and inflation without contract protection as risks. The mechanism is that the same operating leverage works in reverse if volume falls, so margins are defensible in a moderate slowdown but not proven in a downturn. Reported EBITDA also moves with non-cash items: an earn-out fair value gain of USD 8.9 million sits in 2026 reported EBITDA against a charge of USD 29.2 million in nine months 2025, and management's add-backs lift nine-month Adjusted EBITDA USD 27.1 million over reported, so Adjusted EBITDA is the better trend measure but carries management's judgement.

### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is low and is not what limits cash flow: capital expenditure was USD 31.5 million over the last twelve months, 1.95% of revenue, and the issuer does not split maintenance from growth spending, so capex flexibility cannot be separated from growth plans. Working capital is the drain: inventory rose USD 339.2 million since year-end to 55.26% of last-twelve-months revenue, with USD 148.4 million of cash purchases and USD 200.2 million acquired with PAG, and management ties the purchases to a new OEM auxiliary power unit programme and engine initiatives. Interest is the second claim: estimated contractual interest is USD 57.7 million a year before swaps and fees, and cash interest and cash taxes for 2026 are not stated, while FY2025 cash interest was USD 26.8 million and cash taxes USD 16.1 million. Two claims sit outside the debt figure: the earn-out liability of USD 27.4 million, which the issuer may settle in cash or equity, and long-term operating lease obligations of USD 75.8 million; the annual report says finance leases are not material, and the sources mention no pension, factoring or supply-chain finance obligation. Free cash flow was USD 46.6 million in Q3 and USD -50.0 million in the first half, so EBITDA is converting to cash unevenly, and deleveraging over the next four quarters will come mainly from EBITDA growth unless inventory growth stops.

### Competitive forces

Competitive rivalry limits pricing power. The annual report describes a fragmented industry with intense competition, many competitors larger and better resourced than VSE, and OEMs and certified repair facilities that may bundle services. The consequence is that margin gains must come from mix and proprietary repair approvals rather than scale, which is how the third-quarter release frames the Atech purchase, with sole-source repairs on flight-critical parts.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 2

Entry barriers are clearest in repair. Certification and conformance are required before a part is installed, and repairs may be done only at certified facilities with certified technicians, which protects repair margins from new entrants, while the annual report names no comparable barrier for distribution beyond exclusive OEM rights whose duration is not supplied.

The threat of substitutes is modest on the evidence supplied. The annual report names new aircraft components, advanced replacement parts and AI-optimized maintenance as ways competition could change, but shows no loss of volume, so this is a monitoring item and not a driver of the view.

Buyer power centres on concentration. Commercial airlines, MRO integrators and operators buy on availability, turnaround time and price, and one customer group of about 20% of FY2025 revenue could reduce orders or seek relief from its agreements; the 2026 reports do not update that share, so the effect of the PAG purchase on concentration is not established.

Supplier power is material. VSE depends on OEM licences and distribution agreements, on third-party package delivery companies and on suppliers who may be disrupted by tariffs and supply chain delays, and OEMs are also competitors. A non-renewed OEM agreement would hit distribution revenue and the value of the related inventory together, which is why the auditor weighed the effect of exclusive distribution agreements in the inventory assessment.
### PEST factors

PEST factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials. FAA certification rules matter as an entry barrier and are covered under the competitive forces, and the annual report lists tariffs, export controls and the Russia-Ukraine and Middle East conflicts as risks without quantifying any effect on VSE, so no exposure is estimated.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next one to two years reported leverage should fall mechanically as full PAG quarters replace earlier quarters in trailing EBITDA: at the guided year-end Adjusted EBITDA of USD 346.9 million to USD 353.7 million, flat net debt would give 2.58x to 2.53x against 2.98x now. How far leverage falls beyond that depends on inventory and free cash flow, because scheduled amortization is only USD 32.7 million in 2027 and the PAG earn-out of up to USD 125.0 million could take cash if the issuer chooses not to pay in shares. Rates are a headwind: after swaps USD 667.8 million of debt floats, 100 bp higher rates would cost USD 6.68 million a year, and that exposure rises to USD 817.8 million and USD 8.18 million when the USD 150.0 million swap ends on 2027-10-31.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_vse-prxq3x2026earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C11

Over three to five years the debt is back-ended: the amortizing notes of USD 61.0 million at 5.93% end on 2029-02-01, the revolver of USD 500.0 million matures on 2030-05-02, and USD 841.5 million of the term loan B falls due in 2033. The medium-term view therefore turns on whether engine aftermarket demand and OEM programme wins keep earnings growing while the intangible-heavy balance sheet is paid down, and a refinancing in 2032 or 2033 is far enough away to depend on conditions that cannot be forecast from these sources.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-03-31_vsec-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C18

Sector tailwinds named by the issuer are commercial engine aftermarket demand and OEM distribution awards, and sector headwinds are aviation cycles, supply chain disruption and tariffs. Company-specific tailwinds are integration synergies, more repair work done in-house and the proprietary repair approvals added with Atech, and the test capability added with Test Logic; company-specific headwinds are leverage, the inventory build and management's add-backs. Each tailwind supports revenue and margin, and only the integration and in-house repair benefits are within management's control, which makes the fourth quarter the first real check.

### Qualitative downside scenario

The initiating event is a slowdown in commercial engine aftermarket activity, or the loss or reduction of an OEM distribution agreement or of the largest customer group, that sit behind recent organic growth. The first operational break is inventory: USD 893.0 million is 55.26% of last-twelve-months revenue, and if distribution volume falls while purchases tied to distributor agreements continue, stock turns slowly and repair capacity added with PAG is under-used. Revenue and margin fall together because repair capacity and leased facilities are fixed in the short run, and free cash flow turns negative as inventory and receivables absorb cash.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsec-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsec-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C16; calculation C22

The financial transmission is arithmetic on the issuer's own measure: a 10% fall in trailing Adjusted EBITDA with net debt unchanged gives net leverage of 3.31x, a 20% fall gives 3.72x with interest cover of 4.16x on estimated interest, and a 30% fall gives 4.25x; a fall of 25.58% would give 4.00x. These are sensitivities and not forecasts, and no covenant level is supplied to compare them with.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C2

The liquidity effect is limited within two years: USD 545.0 million is 6.03x 2027 scheduled claims, no principal beyond amortization is due before the amortizing notes end in 2029, and the revolver matures in 2030. The refinancing effect arrives through covenants and cost: if the maximum net leverage ratio or the minimum interest coverage ratio tightened, the revolver could be restricted when it is most needed, and a fall in EBITDA would also raise the interest margin on the floating-rate debt, which the credit agreement ties to the leverage ratio. Management's levers are real: it can slow inventory purchases, pay the earn-out in shares, keep the dividend at USD 0.10 per share a quarter, which cost USD 8.0 million over nine months, defer acquisitions and trim capital expenditure of USD 31.5 million. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through the maturity horizon, but not to hold leverage near 3x; the evidence supports no default path and supports a path of slower deleveraging and covenant pressure. Primary downside path: weaker engine aftermarket demand strands inventory and under-uses new repair capacity while debt and interest stay fixed.

### Overall credit view

Overall, VSE presents an adequate business profile supported by an equity-funded balance sheet, exclusive OEM rights and certified repair capability, and record margins, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 2.98x to 3.38x on earnings that include unverified add-backs, free cash flow close to zero and an intangible-heavy asset base. Cash-flow durability is not fully assessable yet because only one quarter has converted well, and the business profile cannot be ranked against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector because no peer data is supplied. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on keeping liquidity of about USD 545.0 million intact, delivering a fourth quarter of strong cash flow and the covenant levels leaving room, with the large maturity in 2033 and the revolver in 2030. The primary downside path is weaker engine aftermarket demand that strands inventory while debt and interest stay fixed. Further analysis would require the credit agreement with covenant levels, the pre-acquisition earnings by acquired business, ratings and market pricing, and the proxy statement. Top risk: leverage that rests on unverified earnings and thin cash conversion.

## Gaps

- High: the executed credit agreement, its first amendment and the note indenture are not supplied, so covenant levels, definitions and headroom are not calculable and the liquidity and leverage judgements stay bounded; the documents would close it.

- High: pre-acquisition EBITDA behind the 2.3x adjusted ratio is not itemized by acquired business, so the gap of USD 88.8 million cannot be tested and the leverage range rests on defined earnings; the acquired businesses' trailing earnings would close it.
